headline: A Dutch company, Intelic, is using AI software to link different drones and air-defence systems so that Ukraine can answer Russian drone attacks faster.
score_reason: New on 8 Oct; a defence-software story with company claims and a test demonstration.
importance_line: Ukrainian forces may be able to react to drone attacks faster by joining many makers' systems into one, and the step toward fully autonomous firing raises questions of human control; the speed claims are the company's own, and a human still decides in the test described.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by Arise News, that Intelic's Nexus software combines radar, sensor and camera data and is now being rolled out in Ukraine; in a late-September test at a former Dutch airbase, a human operator still gave the final order to launch an interceptor drone, though the chief executive said the process could eventually become fully autonomous. Intelic, which holds a €30 million contract with the Dutch Defence Ministry, says the system could cut minutes from the time between spotting a drone and trying to stop it.
notes: Original Reuters link kept as url; text read on Arise News (the Reuters page returned HTTP 401).
